title: MCP Apps on the Stateless Protocol
service: AppBridge: the lesson's MCP Apps server plus a host that reviews UI resources, caches them as content-addressed files, decides what a mounted View may do, runs the postMessage bridge and plans cache invalidation

parts.lesson_anchor: Declare the UI on the tool definition; Fallback is part of the contract; Reject wire ambiguity (-32021 with data.requiredCapabilities); Cache UI resources (a stale iframe must not keep broader permissions); Exercise 1; code/main.py _apps_enabled, tools/list and resources/read
planted_bugs: McpAppServer._apps_enabled looks for io.modelcontextprotocol/ui at the top level of clientCapabilities instead of under extensions; the failure surfaces one call later, as an Apps host getting -32602 Unknown resource URI for the URI tools/list just gave it
McpAppServer._tool adds _meta.ui when the client declared Apps or the server offers them (or instead of and), so every client gets the binding although both peers must opt in
McpAppServer._read folds the missing capability into -32602 Unknown resource URI instead of -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities.extensions naming the extension
AppMount.review re-encodes the 1 MB HTML, recomputes its sha256 and re-reviews the CSP on every View action
parts.timing_assert: 2000 review() calls on a 1,003,800-byte App under 0.05 s. Measured on this machine: the per-action review takes 0.66-2.0 s (13x the limit or more), the review cached per version and admission change 0.4-2.7 ms (18x under it or more)
parts.overfix_guard: a declaration is an object under extensions: a list of names, true, the empty object read as false, only the empty object accepted (a declaration with settings), .get on a list and extensions indexed directly are all caught; an unknown URI stays -32602; a host without Apps still gets the tool without _meta.ui, not an empty list; a cached review must follow replace (narrower CSP, then a version that is not admitted) and withdraw, so a review kept for good, memoized by URI or by digest, kept when the new version fails, reset on replace only, or a digest over a prefix all fail

parts.lesson_anchor: Cache UI resources as executable content: key by canonical ui:// URI, admitted server identity and version, content digest and, when private, the authorization context
parts.storage: content-addressed files: blobs/<sha256 hex of the HTML's UTF-8 bytes> plus an index file
parts.exactness: the content entry round-trips exactly across a reopen: HTML with \r\n, a lone \r, U+2028 and non-ASCII text byte for byte, mimeType text/html;profile=mcp-app, CSP lists in their order with empty lists kept, and other _meta keys

parts.lesson_anchor: The Apps bridge has its own lifecycle; Host context, actions, and revocation (theme and size as changing host context, the host caps the size); code/main.py timeline_html bridge script

parts.lesson_anchor: Cache UI resources as executable content: the four invalidation conditions (ttlMs, binding change, server version or descriptor pin, acknowledged resource-change subscription) and refetch, review and remount

deviations: Part 1: the timing defect sits in the host's per-action check (review.AppMount.review), the code that runs once per View action, not in McpAppServer.handle; the three server defects are the suggested ones, with the binding defect written as 'client declared or server offers' so it reads as the lesson's 'both peers opt in'. The overfix guard covers a new version with a narrower CSP, a version that is not admitted and a withdrawn digest; capability revocation is tested in Part 3, so the same rule is not tested twice.

Part 2: the lookup takes the digest, so the key is exactly the lesson's (URI, server name and version, digest, principal when private); the cache holds no TTL, because expiry is one of Part 5's events. A damaged blob must be repaired by the next put, and a missing blob is a miss.

Part 3: privileged actions get explicit per-call approval in host UI, and a revocation rejects every pending call under the capability for good, so a later grant does not revive them. The load kinds, the device names (camera, microphone, location, as the lesson words them) and the capability names (tools, navigate, clipboard) are this host's names; the lesson does not spell them as keys.

Part 4: send_core only sends; core responses come back as inbox events, so the bridge keeps an in-flight map from core id to View id, and out-of-order and duplicate responses test that mapping. The lesson names only ui/initialize and ui/notifications/initialized; ui/notifications/tool-result, ui/notifications/host-context-changed, ui/notifications/size-changed, the hostCapabilities and hostContext result keys and the theme and size context fields are this host's dialect, stated in bridge.py. Frame timing is checked by recording how many inbox events the bridge had pulled when each frame came out, instead of a timeout.

Part 5: the graph is server, resources (server, uri), cache entries, tools bound to resources, and mounted Views, each mounted from an entry that may have been evicted; a binding event carries only the new URI and the old one comes from the state. Expiry is per entry; the other three events are per resource.

Facts used beyond docs/en.md: the JSON-RPC message text 'Method not found' for -32601 (also in code/main.py); wildcard CSP lists as a hard reject (outputs/skill-mcp-apps-spec.md); the host dialect and names listed for Parts 3 and 4.
